title: System for Activity-aware Fatigue Evaluation (SAFE) framework: Predictive fatigue modelling for occupational tasks
abstract: SAFE framework integrates wearable sensing, biomechanical modelling, and task detection to monitor operator endurance. Validated with 10 participants, it predicts fatigue using IMUs, pressure insoles, and torque-based models, correlating strongly with subjective ratings.
objective: To develop and validate a wearable framework (SAFE) that predicts operator endurance and ergonomic risk using biomechanical modelling and task classification.
methods: Offline lab study with 10 participants performing industry tasks. Used IMUs, pressure insoles, torque-based endurance model, task classification, and custom app. Validated against motion capture and subjective fatigue ratings.
context: Laboratory setting with 10 participants performing industry-type tasks. Focus on occupational ergonomics and fatigue prediction using wearable sensors.
findings: IMU-derived joint angles validated against motion capture with acceptable error ranges.
Framework distinguished high- and low-risk tasks (P < .05).
Strong correlation between predicted endurance and subjective fatigue (r ≥ .878, P < .001).
Task classification via pressure insoles enabled task-specific endurance coefficients.
Framework outputs include predicted ET and CE for real-time monitoring.
System adaptable to dynamic tasks and individual parameters.
future_research: Deploy SAFE for real-time online operator monitoring.
Integrate mobility during tasks for future deployment.
Use perceived exertion to tune model outputs for better validity.
